items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: Well, I think me, Louie, George, and I played a girlfriend.

ctx.x: The head men. The way they used to call them. Peter Hunter. John Rubishow. King Oliver. Louis Armstrong. Fink Martin. You didn't know Buddy Bowling, did you? Yeah, I was a little kid then. Yeah. He stayed at the corner for a while. And one day I was passing and he called me in. And he told me, he said, you drunk brother, isn't he? I said, yes sir. And he said, go down there and get me fifteen cents a beer. And the one time he got him fifteen cents a beer. You know, we used to go there and shoot down, look under…

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: I was playing with Louis to Maine.

ctx.x: Did he, ask him, did he hear the Pillars?

Charlie McCurdy? Wait, let me see. George McCurdy's the man, huh? Yeah. Now, Charlie? Did he play? Soft. Soft. So he played soft. Oh, Charlie, yeah. Charlie used to play with me. But he never did own a band. He used to play with John Robeshoe's band. And that's why I was playing with him. And then from there, Louis the man got him. But he was so soft. After he got off the clarinet, he got on sack. And we thought by him getting on sack, he would blow loud, but it was the same thing. He did kick in, but he was a…
Well, I asked him, did he hear the Peerless band?

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-11
items.q: Cause him and Louis Armstrong was Buddy you know. And you too. Buddy was like that.

ctx.x: I'll say. I'll say. I'll say.

I'll say. I'll say. I'll say. My band was still up then. And that's where I told them we had Maurice and, uh, Rika Ellis. I'll say. Rika Ellis. Rika Ellis. I don't know why Rika left us, but we got, uh, uh, Maurice here. He just come from World of War, you know. First World of War, you know. And then he got in and I'm going to start the bossing, you know. And we said, yeah, we're all young boys, you know, get a band over in the community, try to run all bands along as we've been up. And that's why we kept on and…
I used to lead it for him to catch it. He said, when he catch it, he had a good laugh.
